::: {.cite-bar .domain-war-powers}
[In force]{.status .status-in-force} [20 Stat. 152]{.cite} [18 U.S.C. 1385]{.cite}
:::

A one-sentence criminal statute that bars using federal military forces to execute the laws unless the Constitution or an act of Congress expressly authorizes it.

## Key provisions

- Makes it a crime to willfully use covered armed forces as a posse comitatus or otherwise to execute the laws.
- Does not apply to the National Guard in state status, or to the Coast Guard.
- Operates alongside 10 U.S.C. 271-284, which allow military support to civilian law enforcement short of direct participation in searches, seizures, and arrests.

## Why it matters

It expresses the norm that soldiers do not police civilians. Its practical reach is set by its exceptions, above all the [Insurrection Act](insurrection-1807.qmd).

## Current status

In force. Extended by name to the Navy, Marine Corps, and Space Force by the FY2022 National Defense Authorization Act.
